Alex: Heads up — noticed a jump in unassigned inbound leads in HubSpot over the last 24h. Claim SLA (10m) slipped from ~12% breaches to ~28%. Anyone else seeing this?
Mila: Yep, flagged it in observability this morning :eyes:. Bulk of failures tied to enrichment timeouts — hubspot->enrich webhook returning 504s.
Jamie: I traced it to the enrichment worker pool. When enrichment queue backs up, round-robin assignment skips because the system treats 'enrichment_pending' as unclaimable.
Priya: Quick idea — temporary waitlist fallback: if enrichment pending > 5m, put lead into a "fresh-owner" waitlist that guarantees assignment to an SDR within 10m. Keeps RR fairness but avoids stale-unassigned pile.
Alex: That sounds reasonable. Do we have a simple rule we can push today? Need to avoid double-assigns and keep audit properties.
Jamie: Drafted a lightweight HubSpot workflow + trigger for fallback. Snippet below:
```yaml
trigger: inbound.lead.created
conditions:
  - property: enrichment_status
    operator: equals
    value: pending
  - property: enrichment_pending_seconds
    operator: greater_than
    value: 300
actions:
  - set_owner_pool: fresh-owner-waitlist
  - set_property: fallback_triggered=true
```
Mila: If we do this, add a TTL so fallback owners only have the lead for N minutes before it re-enters RR. Otherwise we skew ownership. Suggest 30m TTL.
Priya: Agreed. Also add a `fallback_reason` property so we can filter in reports: `fallback=enrichment-delay`.
Alex: Can we ship this as a patch behind a feature flag? Want to monitor metrics and rollback quickly.
Jamie: Yup — opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/leadflow/pull/432 (contains workflow + feature flag toggle + telemetry).
Leadbot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for `leadflow/fallback-waitlist` to staging.
Mila: I'll push the flag to staging now and run an A/B sample (10% traffic) to verify delta on claim latency.
Priya: I'll add a short playbook entry in Confluence with steps to revert and checklists for SF/HS sync.
Alex: Action items: Mila = run canary + monitor claim SLA & owner fairness, Jamie = ensure idempotency (no double-assign), Priya = playbook + reporting. Check back in 2h? :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Mila: On it. I'll post initial metrics in this thread.
Jamie: Also adding one more guard: if `owner` field is already set but enrichment later overwrites state, don't move owner. Prevents churn.
Priya: Posted playbook stub: https://docs.redwood.com/confluence/leadflow/fallback-playbook (internal).
Leadbot: deploy-bot: Canary health check passed for 10m. No increased error rate.
Alex: Nice. Thanks team. Let's keep the follow-ups light — if we see new spikes, escalate to eng-sre and tilt RR down while we revert. :thumbsup:
Mila: Noted — will report after 2h check.
